items.text: Confirm docs/specpad/ holds specpad.proj.json, specpad.srs.json, and specpad.vtp.json, and that each parses as JSON.

items.text: Run validate() on a document missing schemaVersion and on one with an unknown type.
items.expected: Each is reported as structurally invalid (non-empty error list).

items.expected: Both are reported invalid, each error naming the missing required field.

items.expected: Each id matches prefix_<6 hex>, and ID_PREFIX maps requirement→r, test→t, heading→h.

items.text: In the VTP editor, set a test's verifies to a requirement and inspect the stored value.
items.expected: The verifies entry equals the requirement's id, not its code label.

items.text: Rename a requirement's code label and re-run governance on a test that verifies its id.
items.expected: The id is unchanged and referential integrity still holds (verifies targets the id, not the code).
items.notes: src/shared/__tests__/governance.test.ts (code-rename / id-immutability case)

items.text: Render the SRS table for a requirement with one, then two, verifying tests and inspect the saved file.
items.expected: The displayed count is computed from verifies (1, then 2); no numTests field is written to disk.

items.text: Inspect a saved SpecPad document for history fields.
items.expected: No modifiedUser, modifiedDate, or change-list keys are present; the file validates.
items.notes: src/shared/__tests__/dogfood.test.ts (validate)

items.text: Call validate() with documents of each type.
items.expected: validate() selects the schema by doc.type and returns [] for each valid document.

items.text: Validate a structurally-correct SRS+VTP pair that has an untested requirement.
items.expected: validate() returns no errors (policy is not its concern); the traceability gap is found only by governance.
items.notes: src/shared/__tests__/validate.test.ts + governance.test.ts separation

items.text: Run checkGovernance on an SRS+VTP pair where one requirement has no verifying test.
items.expected: A traceability violation is reported for the untested requirement.

items.text: Run checkGovernance where a test verifies a non-existent requirement id.
items.expected: A referential-integrity violation is reported for that test.

items.text: Run checkGovernance on a non-heading test whose expected value is empty.
items.expected: A missing-expected violation is reported for that test.

items.text: Run checkGovernance on a bundle whose only untested requirement is a heading.
items.expected: No traceability violation is reported for the heading.

items.text: Compare the shared module's GOVERNANCE_RULES ids against the skill's SKILL.md.
items.expected: Every governance rule id appears in SKILL.md (parity); drift fails the test.

items.text: Round-trip an SRS document through serialize/parse and exercise the fallback download path.

items.text: Render the SRS table with a VTP that verifies a requirement and read the Tests column.
items.expected: The verifying-test count is shown and updates as more tests verify the requirement.

items.text: In the Testing view, change a test's result and save.
items.expected: onSave receives a VTP document with the updated result on the correct item.

items.text: Render the footer status bar for a clean bundle and for one with an untested requirement.
items.expected: The status bar shows "No problems found" when clean and a traceability message when a requirement is untested.

items.text: Run the pre-push hook over synthetic commits in a throwaway repo: no-trailer, trailer+spec, code-without-spec, Spec: none, tag push, and SPECPAD_SKIP.
items.expected: Block on the no-trailer commit; pass on trailer+spec; warn on code-without-spec; no warning with Spec: none; tag pushes (refs/tags/*) are skipped; full bypass with SPECPAD_SKIP=1. Merge commits and pre-adoption history are not policed.

items.text: Inspect SKILL.md for the baseline-generator procedure.

items.text: Inspect SKILL.md for the draft/ratification rule.
items.expected: It states output is a draft for human ratification, never authoritative; generated items are tagged `draft`; deriving from code does not bypass user confirmation.

items.text: Inspect SKILL.md for the distillation altitude and governance-clean rule.
items.expected: It states requirements are at the "shall" altitude (not implementation detail) and the output is governance-clean (verifying VTP entry + expected per requirement).

items.text: Inspect SKILL.md for test mapping and gap handling.
items.expected: It states requirements map to existing tests (named in notes, result reflecting them) and a behavior with no test is recorded as not_tested rather than omitted.

items.text: Inspect SKILL.md for the coverage-reporting rule.
items.expected: It states the generator reports what it covered and could not cover, with no silent truncation.

items.text: Inspect SKILL.md for the requirement-audit procedure.
items.expected: It documents reconciling the SRS/VTP against the whole codebase in both directions, and notes the commit-time audit is the staged-diff form.

items.text: Inspect SKILL.md for the missing-requirement finding.
items.expected: It states code behavior with no requirement is flagged (missing) and a draft requirement plus test is proposed, derived from the code, for ratification.

items.text: Inspect SKILL.md for the stale-requirement finding.
items.expected: It states a requirement whose behavior is gone/changed is flagged stale for update/removal and never silently deleted.

items.text: Inspect SKILL.md for the coverage-gap finding.
items.expected: It states a requirement with no covering test, or a VTP notes reference to a test that no longer resolves, is flagged.

items.text: Inspect SKILL.md for the report/non-destructive rule.
items.expected: It states findings are categorized proposals to ratify, nothing destructive is applied automatically, and coverage/confidence is reported (no silent truncation).

items.text: Render the Auditor view as an orientation index.
items.expected: The Auditor tab renders the scope statement, the design-control map, and the roadmap, with links into the relevant tabs; it does not itself render the trace matrix.

items.text: Confirm the Traceability view reports requirements, test results, and PRD coverage.
items.expected: buildAuditReport returns verified/total requirements, passed/failed/not-tested test counts, and implemented-vs-satisfied plus proposed PRD counts; the Traceability view shows them.

items.text: Confirm the Traceability matrix links PRD→requirement→test with results and flags unverified requirements.
items.expected: Each trace row resolves a requirement's satisfied PRDs and verifying tests with a result rollup; a requirement with no verifying test is rolled up as no_test and visibly flagged in the Traceability tab.

items.text: Confirm the gap list (Traceability) and the roadmap (Auditor).
items.expected: The Traceability view lists checkGovernance violations (and shows governance-clean when none); the Auditor view lists the proposed PRD items as roadmap.

items.text: Confirm the Auditor view shows the scope disclaimer.
items.expected: The view renders text stating SpecPad produces evidence supporting design controls and is not a QMS / compliance determination.

items.text: Confirm the editor classifies and loads a PRD register.
items.expected: classifyDocFilename recognizes <name>.prd.json as a prd document; loadPrd reads it; the Auditor tab is available when an SRS is open.

items.text: Render the design-control map with citations, statuses, and links.
items.expected: The Auditor view lists the formal elements (Design Inputs, Outputs, Verification, Validation, Traceability, Design Changes, Design History File, Design Reviews, Risk Management, Configuration Management), each with an IEC 62304 / 21 CFR 820.30 citation, a statement, a status badge, and a navigation link where applicable.

items.text: Confirm element status is derived from the project.
items.expected: buildDesignControls marks Design Inputs present when requirements exist, Design Verification by coverage, Design Changes present when jobs exist, Design History present when releases exist, and Design Validation / Risk Management as gaps.

items.text: Confirm the visual system is token-based.
items.expected: specpad.less defines CSS custom properties (design tokens) on :root for color/surface/type/spacing, and components reference var(--token) rather than hard-coded values; each theme overrides the same token set.

items.text: Confirm theme selection persists and applies without flash.
items.expected: applyTheme sets data-theme on the document root and writes localStorage; readStoredTheme returns the saved value (default when unset); the three themes are offered; index.html sets the saved theme before the app mounts.

items.text: Confirm the grouped tab order leads with Overview.
items.expected: The tabs read Overview, PRD, SRS, SAD, SDD, VTP, Results, Auditor, Traceability, Releases, Jobs, in that order, and each phase band spans exactly the tabs of its phase.

items.text: Render the Overview with status, latest release, and coverage headline.
items.expected: OverviewView shows the open jobs, the latest release, and a coverage/health headline (verified count and governance findings), with buttons that navigate to the authoring views.

items.text: Confirm Overview is the default view on open.
items.expected: After opening a project, the active view is Overview (the editor's currentView initializes to overview).

items.text: Confirm per-doc-type authoring guides ship and are referenced, not inlined.
items.expected: skill/specpad/guides/{requirements,tests,product-requirements,architecture}.md exist; SKILL.md references each by path; SKILL.md does not inline a guide body (it stays a routing pointer).

items.text: Confirm each guide covers what-to-capture and good/bad examples.
items.expected: Each guide file contains a what-to-capture section and clearly-marked good and bad examples (e.g. ✅/❌ or Good/Bad headings).

items.text: Confirm SKILL.md and the guides stay in sync.
items.expected: The set of guide files under skill/specpad/guides/ equals the set referenced by SKILL.md — no guide is unreferenced and no referenced guide is missing.

items.text: Confirm the skill snapshots before at job creation.
items.expected: SKILL.md's job procedure states that the before snapshot (.specpad/jobs/<id>/before/) is written when a job is created, not only on close; the active job's before snapshot exists and validates.

items.text: Render the active open job's in-progress changes.
items.expected: Given an activeDiffs entry for the active open job (before vs working), the Jobs view detail renders its in-progress SRS/VTP changes instead of the 'materialized once closed' message.

items.text: Render the active open job's in-progress architecture changes.
items.expected: Given an activeArch entry for the active open job, the Jobs view detail renders an Architecture changes section (added/modified/removed files + SAD line diff) for the open job, not only for closed jobs.

items.text: Confirm the document-type registry describes each content type.
items.expected: DOC_TYPES includes srs, vtp, and prd as register kinds, each with a schema, a label, optional/inBaseline flags, and a generate setting; REGISTER_TYPES filters to register kinds.

items.text: Confirm validation and the schema reference are built from the registry.
items.expected: validate() accepts every register type in DOC_TYPES plus the sidecars (project/releases/job/jobs); the generated reference includes each registry type. Adding a type to the registry makes validate() accept it with no edit to validate.ts.

items.text: Confirm the skill snapshots/caches every document in the project index.
items.expected: SKILL.md's refresh and job-cache prose say to snapshot every document in the project index (documents[]) plus the architecture files, iterating the index rather than a fixed list.

items.text: Confirm snapshot/diff are document-type-generic (extensibility).
items.expected: classifyDocFilename recognizes a register type from the registry; a synthetic register type added to the registry is diffed by the shared diffItems and flows through the per-job diff path with no code change; the Jobs view renders a DiffList per register type present.

items.text: Render and edit the Product Requirements tab with status and redline.
items.expected: PrdTable renders the PRD items with an inline status dropdown; changing status/text/tags calls onChange with the updated doc; added/modified rows since the baseline are highlighted (redline); add/delete controls add and remove items; the tab is enabled only when a PRD register is present.

items.text: Confirm the baseline generator drafts PRD + a starter SAD by default (registry-aware).
items.expected: SKILL.md's baseline generator states it drafts the full default set — a PRD (proposed, with SRS linked via satisfies) and a starter arc42 architecture — in addition to SRS/VTP, is registry-aware, and that a type may be declined.

items.text: Confirm init scaffolds the full default set including the PRD.
items.expected: SKILL.md's init scaffolds the full default set; starter.proj.json lists a prd document; a starter.prd.json template ships and is a valid empty PRD; createProjectDoc's default documents are prd/srs/vtp.

items.text: Confirm the PRD tab shows each item's downward trace and flags gaps.
items.expected: PrdTable's Satisfied-by column lists the SRS codes that satisfy each PRD item; a proposed item reads as roadmap; an implemented item with no satisfier is flagged as a gap.

items.text: Confirm a design-control phase band spans the right tabs.
items.expected: ViewTabs renders a phase band per design-control phase; the Design Inputs band spans the Product Requirements + Requirements columns (grid-column 2 / span 2); bands cover Design Verification, Outputs, Controls, Traceability, History, Changes.

items.text: Confirm the working loop directs a job to evaluate impact across every registered document type (not just SRS/VTP).
items.expected: SKILL.md and the CLAUDE.specpad.md template both instruct evaluating the job's impact on every registered document type — naming the PRD (user-facing intent) and the architecture/SAD (structural changes) alongside SRS/VTP — before implementing, spec-first.

items.text: Confirm architecture is a registered (prose) document type.
items.expected: docTypeFor('sad') is defined with kind 'prose' and no schema; 'sad' is absent from REGISTER_TYPES (not diffed as an id-keyed register) yet present in DOC_TYPES (an impactable type).

items.text: Confirm PRD and VTP tables use the SRS interaction model (hamburger + expandable relationship toggle + info-dialog history).
items.expected: PrdTable and VTPTable each render a per-row 'Row actions' hamburger; PRD shows an expandable 'Satisfied by' toggle and VTP an expandable 'Verifies' toggle (collapsed by default); VTP per-item history (attribution) appears in the info dialog, not a column.

items.text: Confirm the PRD table hides Status/Tags and flags proposed items.
items.expected: PrdTable renders no Status control and no Tags column; a proposed item shows a single bold 'PROPOSED' note and its text is italicised; implemented items show no such note.

items.text: Confirm the Verification Tests view shows no execution Result.
items.expected: VTPTable renders no 'Result' column/control; results remain editable only on the Results (TestingView) tab.

items.text: Confirm the software-requirements view is labelled 'Software Requirements'.
items.expected: ViewTabs renders the tab as 'Software Requirements'; the doc-type registry label for srs is 'Software Requirements'; SRSTable's heading falls back to 'Software Requirements'.

items.text: Confirm the document tabs are ordered chronologically by design-control phase.
items.expected: ViewTabs renders tabs in the order Overview, Product Requirements, Software Requirements, Architecture, Verification Tests, Results, Auditor, Traceability, Releases, Jobs.

items.text: Confirm a modified markdown architecture file gets a section-aware diff and diagrams are coarse.
items.expected: mdSectionDiff reports only changed sections by heading with added/removed lines; the Jobs view renders each modified .md file's changed section headings, and reports a changed diagram coarsely as 'diagram changed'.

items.text: Confirm the active job's in-progress architecture diff is section-aware for markdown.
items.expected: The active open job's in-progress architecture changes render the modified SAD's changed section headings and their added/removed lines (section-aware), built from mdSectionDiff over the before snapshot vs the working SAD.

items.text: Confirm the skill documents the release-cut job closing itself as the final step before the release.
items.expected: SKILL.md's 'Cutting a release' procedure states the release-cut job closes itself (status closed) as the last step before the tag, that its version derives to that release, and that an open release-cut job after the release ships is a process error.

items.text: Confirm VTP items carry framework-agnostic automation linkage that validates.
items.expected: A VtpItem with automation [{runner,file,selector}] validates; a RunRecord validates as a sidecar; the matcher resolves links by file/selector.

items.text: Confirm a normalized run record is defined and validates.
items.expected: validate() accepts a run sidecar with runner/ref/ranAt/summary/results and rejects a malformed summary; every run-schema field has a description.

items.text: Confirm automated results derive from the run (and manual falls back).
items.expected: verificationOutcome derives passed/failed/not_run for automated items from the run and ignores a stale stored result; a manual item falls back to its result; rollup counts by status.

items.text: Confirm the Results view groups Manual/Automated tests, shows click-to-edit automation links + a derived status, and omits the verifies trace.
items.expected: TestingView renders a Manual section above an Automated section; an automated test shows its automation link read-only (click reveals inputs) and a run-derived status badge; no Verifies column is present.

items.text: Confirm the skill documents capturing runs and freezing them for deliverables.
items.expected: SKILL.md documents the VTP->test->run chain: the automation linkage, a normalized run sidecar from a machine reporter (framework-agnostic), result derivation, and freezing the run into the release baseline and each closed job's after cache.

items.text: Confirm the run-detail dialog lists the captured run's per-test outcomes.
items.expected: Opening 'View run output' shows the run summary and a per-test table (file, selector, status, duration) with a failures-only filter.
items.notes: run-detail dialog

items.text: Confirm a job's detail shows the run-derived verification status of its changed tests.
items.expected: JobsView's job detail renders a Verification section summarizing the run-derived status (passed/not-run/fail) of the tests the job added/modified, using the job's frozen run or the latest run.

items.text: Confirm roll-ups derive automated results from the run, not a stored field.
items.expected: buildAuditReport derives test pass/fail from the run for automated tests (and falls back to a manual test's stored result); the Overview headline shows the run-derived passing count.

items.text: Validate a jobs register with a record carrying both description and technical_notes; inspect the schema properties; render a job's detail view and confirm technical_notes appears there but not in the list row.
items.expected: validate() accepts a job record with technical_notes; jobsSchema.properties.jobs.items.properties includes both description and technical_notes as optional strings; JobsView's list row renders only description under the title, while the detail view renders a Technical notes field beneath Description.

items.text: Multi-user server (self-hosted)
Start the server against a test repository with no local clone available to the client, and open the editor from the server's own origin.
items.expected: The server serves the version-pinned editor build and its API from one origin; the editor opens the project and lists its documents without any File System Access prompt.

items.text: Request reads and writes for paths outside the allowlist, including traversal forms such as ../../src/index.tsx and an absolute path.
items.expected: Every request resolving outside the configured allowlist is rejected with a client error and no filesystem access occurs; requests inside docs/specpad/ succeed.

items.text: Inspect a provisioned user working tree on disk.
items.expected: The worktree's sparse-checkout cone is the allowlisted paths only; files outside them (for example src/) are absent from the working tree even though they exist in the repository.

items.text: Exercise each API operation named in the transport surface against a test repository.
items.expected: Session, document listing, document read with a version tag, item-operation write, working-copy status, commit, discard, and history passthrough each respond with the documented shape; the listing is derived from the directory rather than a static manifest.

items.text: Inspect the server's imports and assert parity with the shared contract module.
items.expected: The server imports validate and checkGovernance from src/shared and defines no second implementation of either; a parity test fails if the server duplicates a contract rule.

items.text: Start the server with a valid configuration, then with a configuration missing the repository, the branch, and the auth provider in turn.
items.expected: The valid configuration starts; each invalid or incomplete configuration is refused at startup with a message naming the offending setting, and the server does not begin listening.

items.text: Start the server from a configuration file, then start it again with an invalid configuration.
items.expected: The valid run listens and answers requests; the invalid run prints every configuration problem and exits non-zero without listening.

items.text: Build the container image and run it with a config file and a working-directory volume mounted.
items.expected: The image builds; the container serves the editor at its version path and the API on the same origin; the bare clone and per-user worktrees persist in the mounted volume across a container restart.
items.notes: Manual: not automated, and NOT YET RUN — no container runtime was available where the Dockerfile was written. The entry point it packages is the same one boot.integration.test.ts verifies.

items.text: Run the same request flow under two different authentication providers and inspect what the rest of the server sees.
items.expected: Both providers yield a principal with id, display name, email, and groups; the git and document layers behave identically and reference no provider-specific detail.

items.text: Send identity headers from the configured trusted upstream, and then the same headers directly from an untrusted peer.
items.expected: Headers from the trusted upstream establish the principal; identical headers from an untrusted peer are rejected as unauthenticated and never establish an identity.

items.text: Configure the OIDC provider against a test identity provider and complete a sign-in.
items.expected: The authorization-code flow completes without a front proxy and the resulting principal carries the identity provider's name, email, and group claims.

items.text: Start with the development provider bound to loopback, then bound to a non-loopback address.
items.expected: The loopback binding starts and authenticates as the fixed development identity; the non-loopback binding is refused at startup.

automation.selector: refuses the dev provider on a non-loopback bind (AUTH-4)

items.text: Sign in as principals whose group claims map to committer, editor, and reader, and as one matching no mapping.
items.expected: Each mapped principal receives the corresponding role; the unmapped principal is denied access outright rather than defaulting to any role.

items.text: Commit as an SSO-authenticated user and inspect the resulting commit object and the credential used for the push.
items.expected: The commit's author is the authenticated human's name and email; the push is performed with the configured machine credential, and no user credential is required or stored.

items.text: Have two users edit different requirements without committing, then inspect what each user reads back.
items.expected: Each user reads their own uncommitted edits and none of the other's; the two working copies are independent.

items.text: Edit a requirement, close the browser without committing, and reopen the editor as the same user.
items.expected: The edit was autosaved to the user's working copy, is still present on return, and no commit was created.

automation.selector: Repository — status and the pending diff (CMT-2, CMT-7)

items.text: Make several edits and inspect the repository's commit log before and after pressing Commit.
items.expected: No commit exists before Commit is pressed; afterwards exactly one commit on the configured branch contains all the pending changes.

automation.selector: request to commit, over HTTP (CMT-2, CMT-3)

items.text: Attempt to commit a structurally invalid document, and a change introducing a governance violation, under each commit policy setting.
items.expected: A structurally invalid document is never committed; a governance violation blocks the commit under the blocking policy and is reported but permitted under the warning policy.

items.text: Commit with active jobs set, and attempt to commit with none while the policy requires one.
items.expected: The commit's author is the authenticated user and it carries one Job: trailer per active job; with no active job and the policy requiring one, the commit is refused with an explanatory message.

items.text: Advance the target branch between the server's fetch and its push, and observe the retry behaviour and the reflog.
items.expected: The commit is rebased onto the advanced branch and pushed within the bounded retry count; no force-push is ever issued, and a persistent failure is reported rather than forced.

items.text: Open the Commit dialog with pending changes, then use Discard while another user also has pending changes.
items.expected: The dialog lists the pending item-level additions, modifications, and removals together with the governance result before confirmation; Discard restores the user's working copy to the target branch and leaves the other user's pending changes untouched.

items.text: Read a document, let the working copy change, then submit a write carrying the original version tag.
items.expected: The stale write is rejected with a conflict status rather than applied; re-reading yields a fresh version tag with which the write succeeds.

items.text: Have two users edit different items of the same document at the same time, then publish both.
items.expected: Neither write contends with the other — each lands in its own working copy — and both edits survive publication, reconciled by the structural merge with no conflict raised.
items.notes: Supersedes the original item-level-operations wording: per-user working copies remove cross-user write contention entirely, so the reconciliation point is publication, not the write.

automation.selector: merges two people editing different requirements, with no conflict

items.text: Subscribe to the event stream, begin editing an item as a second user, and push a commit to the target branch from outside the server.
items.expected: Subscribers receive a presence event naming the item being edited and, separately, a signal that the target branch has moved.
items.notes: The presence half is exercised end-to-end over a real SSE connection. The upstream-moved half is verified at the unit level (BranchWatcher: first observation is not a change, an unreachable remote is not a change) rather than end-to-end, since that would mean waiting on the poll interval.

items.text: Claim an item, then disconnect abruptly without releasing it; separately, attempt to edit an item claimed by someone else.
items.expected: The abandoned claim expires automatically; the second user is warned but not prevented from editing, and the edit is still applied correctly.

items.text: Inspect the merge module's dependencies and call it with plain document objects.
items.expected: merge is a pure function of base, ours, and theirs, keyed on item id, importing no git or filesystem module; identical inputs always produce identical output.

items.text: Merge one side's change to an item's tags against the other side's change to the same item's text; then merge two different values of the same field of the same item.
items.expected: Different fields of the same item merge cleanly into one item carrying both changes; the same field set to two different values is reported as a conflict naming the item and the field.

automation.selector: merges changes to different fields of the same item without conflict (MRG-2)
reports a conflict when both sides set the same field differently (MRG-2)

items.text: Merge a document where one side deleted an item and the other modified it.
items.expected: The result is a reported conflict for that item; the item is not silently dropped from the merged document.

automation.selector: reports a conflict when one side deletes an item the other modified (MRG-3)
keeps the surviving item when a deletion conflicts with a modification (MRG-3)

items.text: Merge two documents whose items are identical but ordered differently.
items.expected: The merge succeeds with no conflicts and every item is present exactly once.

automation.selector: does not treat a difference in item order as a conflict (MRG-4)

items.text: Force a conflicting rebase of a SpecPad JSON document during a server commit and inspect how it is resolved.
items.expected: Resolution goes through the structural merge; no textual conflict markers ever appear in a document, and the committed file remains valid JSON conforming to its schema.

items.text: Commit a change that conflicts with an upstream change on the same field, and follow the resulting flow in the editor.
items.expected: The server returns a per-field conflict report rather than committing; the editor presents both values for that field and commits the user's choice.

items.text: Run the editor's views against each transport implementation in turn using a shared conformance suite.
items.expected: Every view works unchanged against the local, demo, and remote transports; no view imports a transport module directly, and the conformance suite passes for all three.
items.notes: The conformance suite is table-driven: a transport is verified by adding one entry to TRANSPORTS. All three (local, demo, remote) are covered.

items.text: Open the editor against a server as an authenticated user.
items.expected: The editor fetches the session, and the signed-in user's display name and role are shown in the application shell.

items.text: Open the editor as a reader, as an editor, and as a committer.
items.expected: The reader sees read-only views with no editing affordances; the editor role can edit but is offered no Commit action; the committer sees both. Server-side checks reject writes from a reader regardless of what the client renders.

items.text: Inspect the launcher template and the URL it builds for a project that configures an editor base URL, and for one that does not.
items.expected: The launcher hardcodes no editor host: it carries a placeholder substituted in both the redirect and the no-JavaScript fallback link. A configured base yields <base>/v01/; an absent, blank, or whitespace base yields https://specpad.com/v01/. The version path is always derived from schemaVersion, never taken from the configured base.
items.notes: The skill performs the substitution, so the automated tests cover the template placeholders, the SKILL.md instruction, and the URL-building contract; the scaffold step itself is prose-verified.

items.text: Load a configuration declaring three projects, then one declaring two projects with the same identifier.
items.expected: The three-project configuration validates and yields three project entries, each with its own repository, branch, paths, and credential. The duplicate-identifier configuration is rejected at startup with the offending identifier named.

items.text: Load the existing single-repository configuration, unchanged, from before multi-project support.
items.expected: It validates and produces a one-project deployment with the same repository, branch, paths, and credential; no project identifier is required of the operator.

items.text: Issue API requests with a project segment against a multi-project server, and without one against both a multi-project and a single-project server.
items.expected: A request naming a configured project is served from it. On a single-project server a request with no project segment is served from the only project. On a multi-project server a request with no project segment, or one naming an unknown project, is refused rather than served from an arbitrary project.

automation.selector: routing a request to a project (MPT-3)

items.text: Edit a document as one user in project A without committing, then read and write the same document path in project B as the same user.
items.expected: Project B shows the committed content, not the draft from project A; writing in B leaves A's draft intact. The two projects' working copies are separate directories on disk.

items.text: Sign in as a principal whose groups map to committer in one project and reader in another, against a configuration where a third project declares no role map of its own.
items.expected: The principal may commit in the first project and is refused a write in the second; in the third they hold whatever role the server-wide map grants them.

items.text: Request a project in which the principal holds no role, then request one in which they do, in the same session.
items.expected: The first request is refused with an authorization error and no working copy is provisioned for it; the second succeeds normally.

automation.selector: a role in one project is not a role in another (MPT-6)

items.text: Call the project-discovery operation as a principal with a role in two of four configured projects.
items.expected: Exactly the two projects are listed, each with its display name and the caller’s role and capabilities in it; the other two are absent, not listed-and-refused.

items.text: Subscribe to the event stream for project A while a second user claims an item in project B, then while a third claims an item in project A.
items.expected: The subscriber is not woken by project B's claim; it receives project A's claim. An upstream branch move in B likewise reaches only B's subscribers.

automation.selector: events are scoped to one project (MPT-8)

items.text: Open the editor with a URL naming a project, with a URL naming none against a single-project server, and with a URL naming none against a multi-project server.
items.expected: The first two open the intended project and address the API beneath it. The third reports that a project must be chosen rather than opening an arbitrary one.

automation.selector: asks which project to open rather than picking one or falling back to files

items.text: Inspect the launcher template and the URL it builds for a project index that configures a server project id, and for one that does not.
items.expected: With an id configured, the launcher carries it into the URL it opens and the editor addresses that project. With none, the launcher names no project and the editor opens the server’s only project.

items.text: Sign in to a server hosting several projects and open a different project using only the editor UI.
items.expected: The projects the user may read are offered by name; choosing one opens it. Projects the user holds no role in are not offered.

automation.selector: listing the projects a user may open (MPT-11)

items.text: Switch from one project to another with the switcher, then reload the browser page.
items.expected: The editor's documents, session, and pending-change count are those of the newly-selected project, and the reload returns to that same project rather than the original one.

automation.selector: reloads from the newly-selected project and rewrites the URL to name it

items.text: Open a project on a multi-project server, and on a single-project server.
items.expected: The multi-project editor names the current project; the single-project editor does not clutter the bar with a choice of one.

items.text: Provision a working copy, advance the clock past the configured idle period, and run a sweep.
items.expected: The idle working copy is removed from disk, and a copy used more recently than the idle period is left alone.

items.text: Leave an uncommitted edit in a working copy, advance the clock well past the idle period, and run a sweep.
items.expected: The working copy still exists and the uncommitted edit is intact. Unpublished work has no git object behind it, so reaping it would destroy it outright.

automation.selector: never removes a copy holding uncommitted changes, however idle (WCL-2)

items.text: Reap a working copy, then make an ordinary request as the same user for the same project.
items.expected: The working copy is provisioned again and the request is served normally; the user sees the committed state, with no error.

automation.selector: re-provisions a reaped copy on next use, so the user notices nothing (WCL-3)

items.text: Configure a non-default idle period, then configure reaping off, and sweep in each case.
items.expected: The configured period is honoured; with reaping off no working copy is removed however long it has been idle. An invalid period is refused at startup.

automation.selector: reaps nothing when reaping is disabled (WCL-4)

items.text: Inspect the document-type registry and validate a well-formed detailed design, including a heading-only section and one with no body.
items.expected: The type is registered as an id-keyed register captured in the baseline; a well-formed document validates, and a section with no title is rejected.

automation.selector: SDD — registered as a document type

items.text: Retitle, recode and reorder a design section that a requirement references, then delete a different one.
items.expected: Every reference still resolves after the rename, recode and reorder. Only the deletion breaks a reference, and it is reported as an unresolved design reference.

items.text: Author a design section whose body contains markdown headings and an embedded diagram reference.
items.expected: The document validates and the body is preserved verbatim, including the image reference; nothing in the schema constrains the body to fixed fields.

items.text: Inspect a requirement's design field and the schema that governs it.
items.expected: The requirement carries a list of design section ids; the schema documents them as ids rather than codes, and no reverse link is stored on the section.

items.text: Point a requirement at a design section id that does not exist, with a detailed design present.
items.expected: The unresolved reference is reported against that requirement; with no detailed design present the rule does not run at all.

items.text: Leave one requirement with no design reference, with a detailed design present, and confirm there is no configuration that relaxes the check.
items.expected: That requirement is reported as not reaching the design; headings are exempt; the check applies with no safety-class or documentation-level input available to switch it off.

items.text: Change a design section under a job, then inspect the job's cached before/after and the release baseline.
items.expected: The detailed design appears in the job's before and after snapshots and in the baseline, and the changed section is listed among the job's changes — with no diff, snapshot or view code specific to this document type.

automation.selector: SDD — registered as a document type

items.text: Read the skill procedure for changing a design section.
items.expected: It requires listing the requirements referencing the changed section and deciding for each whether it still holds, in the same job, and says to fix the requirement or the design where it does not.

items.text: Read the baseline generator procedure for drafting a detailed design.
items.expected: It proposes sections from module boundaries, forbids one-per-file across a large tree and decomposition from the call flow, and requires generated sections to be tagged draft for review.

automation.selector: ships a guide for each document type
